newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug stocks jump on strong Q3 earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug stocks jump on strong Q3 earnings.

text.p: Shares in U.S. pharmaceutical companies rallied on Thursday after a string of strong third quarter earnings reports from the group.
"Everybody who has reported so far has had outstanding earnings despite the currency drag," said Gruntal and Co analyst Adam Greene.

Merck and Co Inc, Schering-Plough Corp and Johnson and Johnson on Wednesday surpassed Wall Street expectations with their earnings reports. On Monday Pfizer Inc also reported third quarter results above consensus expectations.

The drug companies have seen their earnings boosted by sales of new drugs that have higher prices and profit margins. Higher sales volume and expense controls have offset the weight of the strong U.S. dollar on foreign sales, analysts said.

Merck was up 2-3/8 to 74-3/8 in afternoon trading. Schroder Wertheim analyst Jami Rubin upgraded the stock to buy from hold, saying the drug maker's third quarter earnings were the strongest it has posted in five years and its near-term outlook is "too strong to ignore."
Johnson and Johnson rose 1-1/4 to 52-1/2 and Schering-Plough added 3/8 to 64-5/8.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Co added 2-3/8 to 103-1/8. It is expected to report earnings on Tuesday driven by sales of its cholesterol-lowering drug Pravachol.

Warner-Lambert Co, also due to report on Tuesday, indicated that its third quarter earnings could be as high as $0.56 a share, above the First Call consensus estimate of $0.54. Its shares rose 3/8 to 65-1/4.
Eli Lilly and Co gained 3/4 to 67-1/2, and American Home Products Corp gained 3/8 to 65. Both are also due to report on Tuesday.
